_doc: Revert-verify mutants for vault-exodev ems__Bug 2e597cb5 (MIN / MAX / SAMPLE answer the group's RDF term, not a new xsd:decimal / xsd:string literal) and ems__Bug 03904911 (SAMPLE does not parseFloat text; SAMPLE of no values is unbound). Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct within the spec). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › <axis> `. Anchors are CODE lines only. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted. Not mutated, on purpose: the QuotedTriple branch of groupValueTerm (no store carrier of an RDF-star term reaches an aggregate — the review found none either) and SAMPLE's "first value" (SPARQL allows any value; locking the first would over-constrain).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/executors/AggregateExecutor.ts

M1_answer_built_from_key._note: The answer is rebuilt from the compared text instead of the chosen term — the pre-fix shape: datatype, language and IRI-ness are lost. G20 (added by the spec): the answer is a NEW literal, so a directional literal loses its base direction.

M2_sample_empty_space._note: SAMPLE of a group without values answers a lone space again (ems__Bug 03904911).
M2_sample_empty_space.to: if (chosen === undefined) return aggregation === "sample" ? new Literal(" ", XSD_STRING) : undefined;

M3_primitive_number_by_js_kind._note: A BIND / expression number answers as the literal of its JS kind (xsd:integer when whole) — the whole result of a division, xsd:decimal by SPARQL, turns xsd:integer in the stored "share by month" queries.
M3_primitive_number_by_js_kind.from: if (typeof term === "number") return new Literal(String(term), XSD_DECIMAL);
M3_primitive_number_by_js_kind.to: if (typeof term === "number") return new Literal(String(term), Number.isInteger(term) ? XSD_INTEGER : XSD_DECIMAL);

M4_expression_text_not_term._note: An expression argument goes through evaluateExpression, which hands a tagged literal over as its text: the tag is lost. G20 (added by the spec): its third form, SAMPLE(COALESCE(?nope, "x"@ar--rtl)), is an expression — through evaluateExpression the direction is lost with the tag.

M5_expression_key_serialized._note: A term yielded by an expression is compared by its N-Triples string (the pre-fix key): MAX(COALESCE(?n, 0)) over 42 and 7 answers 7.
M5_expression_key_serialized.from: const key = typeof term === "object" && "value" in term ? (term as { value: unknown }).value : term;
M5_expression_key_serialized.to: const key = argument.type === "variable" && typeof term === "object" && "value" in term ? (term as { value: unknown }).value : term;

M6_tie_break_dropped._note: Equal keys of different terms keep the first one met — the answer depends on the order the store yields solutions in.
M6_tie_break_dropped.from: keys[i] < keys[best] ? -1 : keys[i] > keys[best] ? 1 : ties[i] < ties[best] ? -1 : ties[i] > ties[best] ? 1 : 0;

M7_max_picks_least._note: MAX keeps the least value — the direction of the extreme is not tied to the aggregation. K9 / K10 / K11 (added by the spec) lock WHICH value MIN / MAX pick — MAX taking the least swaps every pair they check. K12 / K13 / K14 (closure review): the same swap on stored pairs.

M8_empty_text_literal._note: The empty string answers unbound again (the first edition of the prototype) — inconsistent with BIND(""), which holds "" as a value.

M9_values_memo_across_groups._note: Review finding F2 (candidate C2): the argument values are memoised per expression, so every group answers the first group's term.
M9_values_memo_across_groups.to: const memo = ((this as unknown as { __m?: Map<unknown, GroupValue[]> }).__m ??= new Map()); if (!memo.has(expr)) memo.set(expr, this.extractGroupValues(expr, solutions)); return this.computeGroupTermAggregate(aggregation, memo.get(expr) ?? []);

M10_numeric_choice_only_for_numeric_data._note: Review finding F3 (candidate C3): numeric comparison only when every value is a numeric-typed literal — "more SPARQL", but it changes which value is chosen: MAX("10", "9") becomes "9".
M10_numeric_choice_only_for_numeric_data.to: const nums = values.every((v) => typeof v.term === "number" || (v.term instanceof Literal && /#(integer|decimal|double|float)$/.test(v.term.datatype?.value ?? ""))) ? this.asAllNumeric(values.map((v) => v.key)) : null;

M11_evaluation_error_rethrown._note: Review finding F5 (candidate C4): an evaluation error of the argument (?l + 1 over labels) fails the whole query instead of leaving the value out.

M12_blank_node_as_string._note: Review finding F1 (candidate C7): a blank node answers as its text in xsd:string (the pre-fix answer) — isBlank is false and the join back finds nothing.
M12_blank_node_as_string.from: if (term instanceof Literal || term instanceof IRI || term instanceof BlankNode || term instanceof QuotedTriple) {
M12_blank_node_as_string.to: if (term instanceof Literal || term instanceof IRI || term instanceof QuotedTriple) {

M13_ties_ordered_only_when_numeric._note: Review finding F4 (candidate C10): equal keys are ordered by the term only in the numeric branch — equal TEXT of different terms ("abc", "abc"@ru) keeps the first met, and the answer depends on the solution order.

M14_empty_string_excluded._note: Review finding F6 (candidate C6): the empty string is left out of the group — MIN of {"", "x"} answers "x", MIN of {""} is unbound.
M14_empty_string_excluded.to: if (term === undefined || term === null || term === "") continue;

M15_numeric_by_parseFloat._note: asAllNumeric reads text with parseFloat again (the ems__Bug 0c24668f regression). With the fix the dateTime suite of 0c24668f stays green — equal years tie and the tie-break picks the right term — so only text with a numeric prefix shows it: "10 tasks" / "9 tasks", a uid "4ec049e2-…", 3 against an xsd:date (spec review R1).

M16_lexical_by_ntriples._note: The lexical choice compares the term's N-Triples form instead of its text: the closing quote swaps "Task" / "Task!" and "abc" / "abc ", and a bare IRI sorts after a quoted literal (spec review R2). K13: the same swap on stored simple literals; K12: the opening quote of "abc" (0x22) sorts before the "_:" of a blank node, so MIN turns "abc".

M17_lexical_by_locale._note: The lexical choice uses localeCompare instead of UTF-16 code units: MIN of {"apple", "Banana"} turns "apple", MAX of {"Сводка", "Zeta", "ёлка"} turns "Сводка" (spec review R3). K14: the same swap on stored simple literals.
M17_lexical_by_locale.from: keys[i] < keys[best] ? -1 : keys[i] > keys[best] ? 1 : ties[i] < ties[best] ? -1 : ties[i] > ties[best] ? 1 : 0;
M17_lexical_by_locale.to: (typeof keys[i] === "string" ? String(keys[i]).localeCompare(String(keys[best])) : Number(keys[i]) - Number(keys[best])) || (ties[i] < ties[best] ? -1 : ties[i] > ties[best] ? 1 : 0);

M18_direction_dropped._note: A literal answered by the aggregate is rebuilt from value / datatype / language — the base direction is lost: "x"@ar--rtl comes out "x"@ar (spec review R4).

M19_blank_node_key_undefined._note: The comparison key is read as `.value` of ANY object: a blank node has none, its key turns "undefined" and sorts after every text — MIN / MAX of a blank node against "abc" swap (closure review N1).
M19_blank_node_key_undefined.from: const key = typeof term === "object" && "value" in term ? (term as { value: unknown }).value : term;
M19_blank_node_key_undefined.to: const key = typeof term === "object" ? (term as { value?: unknown }).value : term;

M20_ntriples_for_simple_literals._note: N-Triples comparison only for simple literals — exactly the form vault text is stored in; VALUES literals (xsd:string) keep passing K10 (closure review N2). K12: the stored "abc" is a simple literal, its N-Triples quote sorts before the blank node's "_:" — MIN turns "abc".
M20_ntriples_for_simple_literals.to: const keys = nums ?? values.map((v) => (v.term instanceof Literal && !v.term.datatype && !v.term.language ? v.term.toString() : String(v.key)));

M21_locale_for_simple_literals._note: localeCompare only for simple literals — the stored form; VALUES literals keep passing K11 (closure review N2).
M21_locale_for_simple_literals.from: keys[i] < keys[best] ? -1 : keys[i] > keys[best] ? 1 : ties[i] < ties[best] ? -1 : ties[i] > ties[best] ? 1 : 0;
M21_locale_for_simple_literals.to: (typeof keys[i] === "string" && values[i].term instanceof Literal && !(values[i].term as Literal).datatype && !(values[i].term as Literal).language ? String(keys[i]).localeCompare(String(keys[best])) : keys[i] < keys[best] ? -1 : keys[i] > keys[best] ? 1 : 0) || (ties[i] < ties[best] ? -1 : ties[i] > ties[best] ? 1 : 0);
